title: Cover versions of Billboard's top twelve for Germany and Japan
summary: Lee produced weekly top-twelve cover records for export, such as Honey, and the German studios sent back superior-sounding copies.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now, what happened was I was doing -- there was a time in between jobs where I was doing -- I used to do for about a year for Germany and Japan the top 12 hits of Billboard. I had a deal with the guy who used to ship them to Japan, and Germany -- but it would be the top 12 of Billboard.

Now what you had to do -- I would do this every week, the top 12, but I got better at that than I am at the racing form, you know? Because you got to guess what's gonna end up being up there. See, if you record the 12 this week, now you know some of those songs remain the next week. Now I've got to get 12 for the next week, and I have to have them every week. So you had to really live with the charts, and try to decide what's gonna be there 3 weeks from now. You know? And you'd be surprised what kind of record -- I had doing that thing.
I got so good at it -- really -- there was one song that came on the charts, what's the guy's name, it was about his wife, one of the best songs -- it jumped; it came on, like,

50, and then it went to like, 10 -- and do you know, I recorded it the second week. "Honey" -- that was it. It was a smash. "Honey" -- just a great song, and it just took the 2nd week, I grabbed it, and it jumped up there, you know, and I heard every record -- heard more records then than I do now, you know; had to listen to everything. We did things -- Aretha was hot then; and I kept a stable.

I had a male singer, a female singer, a female group, a male group and a 6 piece band -- and we would go in every Saturday, every Saturday -- and made quite a bit of money with it. Made quite a bit of money with it. Did it for about a year and 3 months.
Was that somehow related to the ....

Yes. Better finish the story. Why it's related to the German studio, when we used to send these tapes to Germany and send them to Japan, the German people started sending us things back, and telling us what was wrong with our sound, and would play things and send them back on the tape and tell us, this is what it should sound like, and it was no comparison. The fidelity, you would not believe. You would not believe it. I mean, just unreal. Unreal. They would copy, I'm saying, the stuff that I had sent them -- and when they got through turning their knobs, whatever their knobs had on them, they never asked us to play what we sent them and play what they sent us back also. Then you just wouldn't believe it.
